title: U.S. House · Arizona's 3rd District
area: West-central Phoenix metro area, including parts of west and south Phoenix, Tolleson, Avondale, and parts of Glendale.

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Yassamin Ansari, first elected in 2024, won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed. No Republican candidate advanced from the primary ballot; write-in candidate Nicholas Glenn received 437 write-in votes but did not meet Arizona's minimum vote threshold to advance to the general election. Jacob Parkman is running as a Republican write-in candidate in the general election. David Redkey won the Green Party primary and Alan Aversa won the No Labels Party primary. Cook Political Report rated the district D+22, and Democrats were guaranteed to win a seat here in 2026 since no Republican qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Yassamin Ansari
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Yassamin Ansari is the Democratic incumbent for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024 to succeed Ruben Gallego, who ran for U.S. Senate. She worked as a policy advisor, including in the office of the UN Secretary-General, and served on the Phoenix City Council, where she became vice mayor. In the House she serves on the Natural Resources and Oversight and Government Reform committees.

background.text: Born in Seattle, Washington, to parents who immigrated from Iran; grew up in Scottsdale, Arizona, and attended Chaparral High School, according to Wikipedia.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Stanford University in 2014 and a master's degree from the University of Cambridge, where she was a Gates Cambridge Scholar. Her office describes her as a daughter of immigrants and a graduate of both universities.

Began her career at the United Nations, working in the office of Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon as a senior policy advisor, including on the Paris Agreement, and later in the same role under Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

Elected to the Phoenix City Council (District 7) in a March 9, 2021 runoff and took office April 19, 2021. Her official biography says she was the youngest woman ever elected to the council and later served as vice mayor.
On the council she created the city's Office of Heat Response and Mitigation. She resigned her seat on March 28, 2024 to focus on her congressional campaign.
Announced her run for Arizona's 3rd District on April 4, 2023, won the 2024 Democratic primary by 39 votes, and won the general election with nearly 71% of the vote, succeeding Ruben Gallego.

Sworn into the U.S. House in January 2025 as the youngest woman in the 119th Congress and, according to her office, the first Iranian American Democrat in Congress. Serves as Freshman Class President for House Democrats.

Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources, where she is Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee, and the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. In 2026 she advanced from the Democratic primary with 100% of the vote.

priorities.text: Rep. Ansari believes that the climate crisis is the defining issue of our generation... In Congress, Rep. Ansari serves on the House Natural Resources Committee and as the Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee where she is committed to working with her colleagues on legislation to combat climate change and build a more sustainable future.
Rep. Ansari knows that housing is a human right, and she is fighting to lower the costs of rent and housing across the board.

positions.summary: Has cosponsored legislation opposing withdrawal from the Paris Climate Accords and supporting clean energy jobs, and works on climate legislation as Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee.
positions.quote: Since being sworn in, Rep. Ansari has cosponsored legislation disapproving of President Trump's withdrawal from the Paris Climate Accords, supporting energy resiliency, protecting our federal lands, and advocating for clean energy jobs.

positions.summary: Says the district does not have enough housing to keep up with population growth and has pushed for additional federal housing funding.
positions.quote: In places like Arizona, Rep. Ansari knows we don't have nearly enough housing to keep up with our growing population. That means the cost of living is higher, rent is going up, and we've seen a spike in homelessness which is hurting families and our economy.

positions.summary: Says the country can have both a secure border and be pro-immigration; has introduced a resolution opposing discriminatory immigration policies and backed the American Dream and Promise Act while also saying she supports securing the border.
positions.quote: Rep. Ansari believes that we can have a secure border, be pro-immigration, and have an economy that works for everyone.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee; Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs Subcommittee), the House Committee on Natural Resources (Energy and Mineral Resources; Oversight and Investigations), and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Introduced a resolution celebrating the contributions of immigrants and opposing discriminatory immigration policies, her first piece of legislation in Congress.

candidates.name: David Redkey
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Green Party primary as a write-in candidate

summary.text: David Redkey is the Green Party nominee for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District. He also sought the Green nomination in the 1st District. In a Ballotpedia survey for that race he describes himself as a public-school teacher, small business owner, and disability advocate focused on conservatorship reform and what he calls "Foundational Economics."

background.text: Born in Bloomington, Indiana. Attended Sunnyslope High School; earned an associate degree from Glendale Community College in 2014, a bachelor's degree from Arizona State University in 2016, a master's degree from Arizona State University in 2019, and a graduate certificate from Northern Arizona University in 2023.
Describes himself as a public-school teacher, small business owner, and disability advocate who runs TBI Writer LLC.
Says his experience with the Arizona probate system after a debilitating injury led him to advocate for conservatorship reform, and that he serves as director of Clean Up Our Courts Arizona.
Advanced as the Green Party nominee for Arizona's 3rd District in the July 21, 2026 primary as a write-in candidate with 5 votes. Says he lives in Arizona with his wife and son.

candidates.name: Alan Aversa
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 No Labels Party primary

summary.text: Alan Aversa is the No Labels Party nominee for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District. He describes himself as a teacher with a physics and astronomy degree from the University of Arizona, and has appeared on Arizona ballots under other party labels.

background.text: Born in Ashland, Oregon. Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona in 2008, in physics and astronomy with minors in math and Italian, according to his 2022 Ballotpedia survey.
Has worked as an educator, teaching physics and computer programming in classrooms and online; in a 2023 survey he described himself as a middle school science teacher.
Ran unopposed in the 2012 Republican primary for Arizona House of Representatives District 3, and advanced from the Green Party primary for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District in 2024 with 29 votes.
Is the No Labels Party nominee in 2026, advancing from that party's primary on July 21, 2026. In earlier surveys he listed right to life as a priority.

candidates.name: Jacob Parkman
candidates.ballotNote: Running as a Republican write-in candidate in the general election; no Republican qualified for the primary ballot

summary.text: Jacob Parkman is running as a Republican write-in candidate for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District, after no Republican met the vote threshold to advance from the primary. He holds a Ph.D. in chemistry and has taught at the high-school, community-college, and university levels.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Boynton High School, a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University-Idaho in 2015, and a Ph.D. from Brigham Young University in 2023.

Has worked as an adjunct professor. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a husband, father of six, educator, and scientist with a Ph.D. in chemistry who has taught at the high-school, community-college, and university levels.
Describes his faith in Jesus Christ as the foundation of his values. Is running as a Republican write-in in the November 3, 2026 general election.

researchNotes: This district was guaranteed to Democrats in 2026 because no Republican candidate met Arizona's write-in vote threshold in the primary; Jacob Parkman is instead running as a write-in candidate directly in the general election. No campaign website or detailed public statements were found for David Redkey, Alan Aversa, or Jacob Parkman beyond Ballotpedia's electoral records within this research session's time budget; their entries are marked minimal. Yassamin Ansari's specific issue positions were not found on Ballotpedia beyond biography and committee assignments; her federal floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script per the division-of-labor guidance. Biographies for Alan Aversa and Jacob Parkman come only from their Ballotpedia profiles and survey responses; David Redkey's from his Ballotpedia profile and a survey filed for the 1st District race.
